title: Session slab ops cheatsheet - Sonia
content:
Quick personal slab for session experiments - keep this short and messy. Used during 1:1s and quick pairing when iterating cache+batch heuristics.

GOAL: find config with median latency <= 120ms for seq<=1024 while keeping token cost under target and KV cache hit >= 85%.

Legend:
- med = rolling median over 50 requests
- p95 = 95th percentile (sample window ~2k reqs)
- kv_hit = % of requests served from KV prefix cache (measured by tag on trace)
- cost_est = rough cost per 1k tokens (in platform units) based on GPU/unit-time and token rate

--- runs table (quick) ---
| run_id | date | model | quant | batch | seq_len | tokens | med_ms | p95_ms | kv_hit | notes |
| R-210 | 2025-04-02 | redwood-v2-7B | int8 | 8 | 512 | 3200 | 138 | 240 | 71% | baseline - no prefix prewarm |
| R-211 | 2025-04-03 | redwood-v2-7B | int8 | 8 | 512 | 3200 | 112 | 190 | 88% | enabled prefix prewarm (warm-first-req) |
| R-214 | 2025-04-07 | redwood-v2-7B | int8 | 16 | 256 | 2400 | 96 | 160 | 80% | higher batch -> med drops, p95 improved too |
| R-218 | 2025-04-10 | redwood-v2-7B-fp16 | fp16 | 8 | 1024 | 6400 | 160 | 320 | 65% | fp16 higher memory pressure, lower kv hit (evictions) |
| R-225 | 2025-04-18 | redwood-v2-7B | int8+kv-opt | 8 | 512 | 3200 | 106 | 178 | 91% | tuned KV stable windows, candidate winner for low-latency tier |

Notes on table: numbers are from synthetic harness in /bench/sess-slab/quick-run. med_ms is the 50-req rolling median sampled every 30s during the 10m run. p95 measured at the end. kv_hit defined as cache read success for prefix tokens.

Quick cost back-of-envelope:
- baseline GPU cost: 0.45 units / GPU-minute (test env)
- average tokens/sec per GPU (R-211): ~530 toks/s -> ~31.8k toks/min
- cost per 1k tokens = 0.45 / 31.8 = 0.01415 units (~0.014)
- so 10k tokens ~0.141 units. (use for rough comparisons between runs)

Immediate takeaways:
- prefix prewarm increases kv_hit by ~15-20pts and reduces median latency by ~20-30ms for these seq lengths.
- bumping batch to 16 helps median but watch p95 if per-request variability increases.
- fp16 option reduced compute time per token but caused cache churn (evictions) -> net worse p95. Need larger kv-window or pin-lru.

Open questions / quick TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run R-214 with batch=12 and measure p95 (middle ground). (ticket ENG-1503)
- [ ] Add a short experiment to measure cold-start penalty for prefix prewarm (vary prewarm tokens 8/16/32).
- [ ] Confirm cost numbers on staging (this sheet uses harness GPU pricing, not production).
- [ ] Try kv window size=4k tokens to reduce eviction under fp16.

Tiny checklist for next session:
- copy R-225 config to canary route (dev-rc)
- run 30m canary with real user traces (sampled)
- snapshot traces and mark examples where kv_hit=false and med>150ms

Scratch math (quick):
- Rolling med improvement from R-210 -> R-211 = 138 -> 112 ms = 26 ms (~19% improvement)
- kv hit improvement = 88 - 71 = 17 pts; suggests prewarm success correlates strongly with med drop.

Useful links:
- profiling harness: gs://redwood-bench/sess-slab/ (notes in Confluence too)
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/932 (kv prewarm patch)
- e2e test case: jira ENG-1427 (kv eviction reproducer)

Random scratch:
- if med target is 120ms, R-211 (112ms, 88% kv) is promising but p95=190ms -> need to keep p95 < 250ms for SLAs. Good.
- want kv_hit >= 90% ideally; R-225 hits 91% but verify over longer windows.

Notes-to-self: keep this file lean. Move polished tables to /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/bench-reports when ready.

End of sheet.
